title: Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
abstract: arXiv:2611.33394v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated decision-making. However, LLMs may produce incorrect answers with high confidence, limiting their applicability in decisions that affect individuals and organizations. Reliable confidence scores are necessary to gate such decisions, and existing estimates are frequently unavailable or too coarse to support effective gating. This work uses supervised learning to train models to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, enabling automated confident responses and routing uncertain ones for human review. A linear confidence score head is fitted to the final-layer hidden state of the frozen LLM backbone, and text-only metamodels are trained as an alternative for closed models. tldr: 该论文提出利用监督学习在冻结LLM的最终层隐藏状态上拟合线性置信度分数头（并为闭源模型训练仅文本的元模型），以预测LLM答案的正确性，从而实现高置信度回答的自动化处理和不确定回答的人工审查分流。
